spans.s: + अर्थिन् भार्या- + अर्थिन्, adj. desiring a wife,
+ दारक भर्तृ- + दारक, 1. m. a young prince, designated as suścessor. 2. f. का, a princess.

भर, i. e. भृ + अ,
 I. m.
 1. A load,

; Vikr. d. 42; 52; with भुवस्, ἄχθος ἀρούρας i. e. a dead mass.
 2. With कृ, To make a load, to support one's self,

. A measure of value of two thousand Palas.
 II. adj. Who or what supports.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Lat. -fer; A.S. -bora.

भार, i. e. भृ + अ, m.
 1. Carrying burthens, Pañc. i. d. 312.
 2. Weight, a burthen, Pañc. 52, 4; figurat., Pañc. 31, 3 (of government); v. d. 4.
 3. A great weight, Pañc. 99, 25.
 4. A weight of gold equal to two thousand

भरण, i. e. भृ + अन,
 I. n.
 1. Bearing, Pañc. 257, 23; supporting, Śāk. d. 192.
 2. Nourishing, Hit. ii. d. 42.
 3. Wages, hire.
 II. f. णी.
 1. The name of the second lunar asterism.
 2. A creeper, commonly Ghoshā.
भरण्ड (vb. भ्रि). m. A master, a lord.
भारण्ड, भारुण्ड भारुण्ड, भेरण्ड भेरण्ड (m.), The name of a fabulous bird, see Pañc. 263, 19; cf. my translation, 535, n. 1437. f. दी, Its female, Pañc. 264, 4.
भरण्य (for भरणीय, ptcple. of the fut. pass. of भृ), n. Wages, hire.

भरत, i. e. भरन्त्, ptcple. pres. of भृ, + अ (cf. Śāk. d. 192), m.
 1. The name of several princes, and of a sage, the inventor of dramatic composition, Vikr. d. 36; Utt.

भारत, i. e. भरत + अ,
 I. patronym. A descendant of Bharata, Hit. iv. d. 86.
 II. m.
 1. An actor.
 2. A name of fire.
 III. f. ती.
 1. Speech,

. Dramatic recitation.
 3. The goddess of speech, Pañc. ii. d. 16.
 4. A quail.
 IV. n.
 1. India proper.
 2. A great epic poem, also महाभारत महा-, n.
भरथ, m. A deity presiding over one of the regions.
भरद्वाज, i. e. भरन्त्, ptcple. pres. of भृ, -वाज, m. The name of a Muni, Johns.

भारद्वाज, i. e. भरद्वाज + अ,
 I. patronym., m.
 1. Epithet of []

. The son of Vṛhaspati.
 II. m. A skylark, Pañc. 157, 3, Wild cotton.
 IV. n. A bone.
भरित, i. e. भर + इत, adj. Filled,
or भरीमन् भरी̆मन् (vb. भृ, or भर, + इमन्), m. A household, a family.

भरु, i. e. भृ + उ, m.
 1.
भरु-ज, m. A small sort of jackal.
भर्ग, i. e. भ्राज्, or भृज्, + अ, m. Śiva.

भर्गस्, i. e. भ्राज्, or भृज्, + अस्, n.
 1. Light,

= Rigv. iii. 62, 10.
 2. A name of Brahman.
 --Cf. A.S. baelch, superbia.

भर्तृ, i. e. भृ + तृ,
 I. m., f. त्री, and n.
 1. One who contains, Śiś. 9, 17.
 2. A cherisher,

. A protector.
 II. m.
 1. A lord, Vikr. d. 36; master, d. 155.
 2. A commander,

. A husband, Hit. i. d. 196, M.M.
 --Comp.

-भर्तृ + क, latter part of comp. words, which are, or were originally adj.; e. g. प्रोषित- (ptcple. of the pf. pass. of प्र-वस्), f. का, A woman whose husband is absent, Ṛt. 6, 9. स-, f. का, A woman whose husband is alive.
भर्तृ-घ्न + त्व, n. Injuring one's master,
भर्तृ + मन्त्, adj., f. मती, Married, Śāk. d. 114.
भर्तृ-हरि, m. The name of a prince and poet.

भर्त्स्, i. 10, Ātm. (also Par.).
 1. To menace, Daśak. in

.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. भर्त्सित, Blamed, Pañc. i. d. 170. n. Menace, Daśak. in

.

(read ˚भर्त्स्-अयत्).
 --With नि नि, To menace, Pañc. 220, 2 (probably corr. निर्भ्˚).
 --With निस् निस्,
 1. To menace, Pañc. 84, 18;

.

भर्मन्, i. e. भृ + मन्, n.
 1. Wages, hire.
 2.

. A coin, a piece of money.
 4. The navel.
 --Comp.
भर्व्, and † भर्भ् भर्भ्, or † भर्ब् भर्ब्, i. 1,

. To injure (ved.).
 2. † To eat.
 --With the second signification and the form भर्ब् cf. ϕέρβω, ϕορβή; Lat. herba; with the first and भर्व् Goth. balvjan.
भारवि, m. The name of a poet,
भारिक, i. e. भार + इक, m. A porter,
(treasurer; cf. 176 and my Chr. p. 315, n. ad 176. I propose to read भौरिक).
भारिन्, i. e. भार + इन्, m. A porter,

भार्गव, i. e. भृगु + अ, patronym.
 I. m.
 1. A descendant of
. A name of Śukra, regent of

. An archer.
 5. An elephant.
 6. A proper name, Johns.

भार्या, properly ptcple. fut. pass. of भृ, f. A wife, Pañc. 137, 9.
 --Comp.
भार्याट, m. A man who lets out his wife for prostitution.
भार्या + त्व, f. State of a female,
+ यष्टि भार- + यष्टि, f. a yoke or pole for carrying burthens.
+ वाह भार- + वाह, m. a porter.

+ वाहिक भार- + वाहिक,
 I. adj. carrying burthens.
 II. m. a porter.
कुरु-, भरत-, भृगु- + श्रेष्ठ कुरु-, भरत-, भृगु- + श्रेष्ठ, m. an excellent descendant of Kuru, Bharata, Bhṛgu,
